components.title: Burnout features

rows: Write down the top 3 work stressors and 1 thing you can pause or delegate this week
Set a firm start and stop time for work, and protect a real break away screens
Use 0 minutes of movement, such as walk or stretching, to interrupt tension
Try one calming practice such as slow breathing, mindfulness or meditation, for 5 to 10 minutes
Ask one trusted person for support and talk through what feels hardest
Review sleep habits and aim for a consistent bedtime and wake time
Reassess your workload and decide what needs a manager conversation or longer-term change

rows: may help if symptoms last more than a short period, interfere with daily life, or start affecting sleep, mood, or physical health. It is especially important to seek help if you feel hopeless, cannot function at work, are relying on alcohol or drugs to cope, or think the problem might be depression or another mental health. NHS guidance says to speak with GP or contact talking therapies if burnout is affecting daily life mental health.
